answer: Each registered oasis keeps a lotus pond with a gauge and camera. An epoch opens only during a comet's predicted pass, an 18-minute window from public ephemeris. At dawn the lotus blooms once pond water crosses 26C, and the agent submits one timestamped photo of the open bloom, gauge reading, and comet trail, checked against satellite weather. Cloning 100 oases costs $800 a pond, $150 lotus stock, $90 gauge, $120 camera, $300 monthly lease each, plus 80,000 POA locked 45 days and 40,000 POA burned per clone. A lotus opens only where the water is real; a comet keeps only its own clock.
